title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & parallelism
author: Ava Chen
release_notes: Split the monolithic CI workflow into separate lint, test, and release pipelines; improved caching and parallelism heuristics resulting in ~35% faster CI runs on common PRs and reduced CI cost. No behavioral changes to runtime code. Recommended to monitor flakiness dashboards for two weeks after rollout.
description: Context: Our consolidated GH Actions workflow has grown complex and is slowing down PR feedback loops. This PR splits lint, unit/integration test, and release automation into separate workflows and standardizes caching and parallelism settings across the monorepo. Goals: 1) reduce PR latency by allowing independent lint/test runs to proceed in parallel, 2) improve cache hit rates across packages, 3) simplify release automation and make it easier to iterate on release steps, 4) reduce CI cost and improve observability. Changes: - Introduced three top-level workflow files: .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml. - Consolidated shared reusable job steps into .github/workflows/actions/common.yml and referenced via uses:. - Improved dependency cache keys to include package-lock.json/poetry.lock/yarn.lock where applicable and added cross-repo cache splaying to better reuse action caches. - Tuned matrix and parallelism heuristics: smaller matrices for quick PRs, dynamic job-level parallelism for heavy integration tests. - Reworked workflow triggers: push/pr branch filters to avoid redundant runs on release-automation pushes; scheduled nightly full-test suites. - Updated various build scripts and CI helper npm/python packages (ci-utils) and bumped node to 20 in CI containers. Migration notes & checklist: - [x] Split workflows created and validated locally.- [x] Lint and unit tests green on representative PRs across redwood, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript.- [x] Release workflow tested in a dry-run namespace and validated artifact signatures.- [x] Observability: added metrics/logging points to CI self-metrics and created an alert to detect >15% failure rate post-rollout. - [x] Updated docs: CONTRIBUTING.md CI section and internal runbook. Impact: Merged changes should reduce median CI time for PRs touching a single package from ~19m to ~12m and reduce overall runner minutes by ~20% in our sample week. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable workflows for all repos, monitor CI dashboard for 48 hours, revert gate if failure rate spikes. Related: ENG-2298 (CI latency), ENG-2312 (release automation hygiene).
